title: Anthropic's text watermarks signal new front in AI detection
candidate_claim: Reporting describes Anthropic marking new-model outputs globally in connection with EU transparency rules.
notes: Treat product scope and performance as reported until verified in first-party technical material.

title: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
candidate_claim: EU Article 50 guidance describes machine-readable, detectable marking obligations subject to technical feasibility and exceptions.
notes: Official explanatory guidance; it notes that its summary is not legally binding.

title: China releases Measures for Labeling AI-Generated and Synthetic Content
candidate_claim: Chinese authorities announced measures and a mandatory standard covering explicit and implicit labels, effective 2025-09-01.
notes: Official Chinese source; use translated summaries cautiously and do not infer enforcement outcomes.

title: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content: An Overview of Technical Approaches to Digital Content Transparency
candidate_claim: NIST distinguishes provenance, watermarking, labelling, detection, auditing, and authentication as separate approaches.
notes: Technical synthesis; it does not settle their social effects.

title: Frontier Research on Mitigating Risks from Synthetic Content: A Call to Action
candidate_claim: NIST identifies robustness, security, international adoption, and information-ecosystem effects as open challenges.
notes: Useful for limits; it is not evidence that a given system fails in a given context.

title: Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content
candidate_claim: The Commission published a voluntary code to support providers and deployers meeting Article 50 obligations.
notes: A voluntary code is neither direct evidence of universal uptake nor a guarantee of interoperable implementation.
